questions.question: According to the speaker, what does the market primarily consider when pricing an asset?
questions.answer: What is expected to happen in the future.
questions.explanation: The excerpt states that an asset price is a lot about pricing today, things that you expect to happen in the future (Q0010).

evidence.quote:
An asset price is a lot about pricing today,
 things that you expect to happen in the future.

original_segments.text: And then they expect quickly the Fed to start undoing that.
That's what this path is telling you.
This is a expected policy rate path.
What the market thinks now, the policy rate
will be in the next meeting, two meetings from now,
three meetings from now, four meetings of the FOMC from now.
Well, if you look at the same picture in Europe,
it looks like that.
It's clear that there is more ahead.
And you see that's what the market perceived at this point.
Whether that ends up being true or not doesn't matter.
At any point in time, the exchanges
determine where the markets think.
So what actually happens is less important for an asset price.
An asset price is a lot about pricing today,
things that you expect to happen in the future.
What you expect is what matters, not what
actually happens, and at this moment,
the market expects the euro area to go
through a more prolonged period of hiking, interest rate
hiking.
